items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: There was the name of the hall and the date of the dance and in big letters "Professor Johnson Coleman" and his band.

ctx.x: Two weeks later we went back to Richmond and then the organizer told me that he would like me to be the leader of the orchestra the next time they had a dance. There was one about three weeks after that and I took Edgar Courance who was still playing C melody sax, William Smith on piano, Wilbur Cocksey, alto and Edgar James, drums.

When we arrived in Richmond and I saw the advertising bills and posters for the dance, I wasn't happy about the way they had been made. There was the name of the hall and the date of the dance and in big letters "Professor Johnson Coleman" and his band. I did not like the idea of me being called "Professor" because my idea of professor was an older person than I was and in the case of being a musician, a professor was one that knew all about music and was also a music teacher.

But I had been billed that way and although I played the best I could that night, every time someone called me "Professor" I would tell them that I was not a professor. We played Richmond a few more times and no matter how hard I begged the organizers not to put "Professor Johnson Coleman" on the posters, every time we went there, it was "Professor Johnson Coleman". I really never considered myself a leader to the extent of getting more money than the rest of the musicians, so we all had the same pay when the job…
